What causes kala-azar, and what is its vector?
Leishmania donovani, transmitted by the sandfly (Phlebotomus).
What is the main endemic area of kala-azar in Sudan?
Eastern Sudan (Gedaref, Sennar and Blue Nile).
What are the clinical features of kala-azar?
Fever for more than 2 weeks, wasting, massive splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, pallor and bleeding.
What are the blood findings in kala-azar?
Pancytopenia, a high ESR, high gamma globulin and low albumin.
What are the common causes of death in kala-azar?
Bleeding, secondary infection, severe anaemia and malnutrition.
What is the clinical case definition of kala-azar?
Fever for more than 2 weeks, with splenomegaly or enlarged lymph nodes and weight loss, in a person from an endemic area.
What is the first serological test for kala-azar?
The rK39 rapid test (or the direct agglutination test, DAT).
What is the most sensitive parasitological test for kala-azar?
A spleen aspirate for Leishman–Donovan (LD) bodies, which is about 95% sensitive.

What is the regimen of sodium stibogluconate (SSG) with paromomycin?
SSG 20 mg/kg/day with paromomycin 15 mg/kg/day intramuscularly for 17 days.
What is monitored during treatment with sodium stibogluconate?
The ECG, because of cardiotoxicity, and pancreatitis.
How are severe visceral leishmaniasis, relapse and HIV co-infection treated?
With liposomal amphotericin B (combined with miltefosine in HIV infection).
What supportive care is given in kala-azar?
Nutrition, blood transfusion, and treatment of infections and malaria.
